Title: Gaussian squared-norm inflation (expectation-level)
Statement_Strength: Exact equality in expectation given the stated construction; per-realization only a probabilistic/concentration statement
Assumptions: Noise norm fixed at rho*||Delta|| by construction (verified against src/attacks/traceability.py); noise direction uniform on unit sphere and independent of Delta; per-realization concentration claim additionally assumes high dimension d (this project: d=11220132)
Proof_Status: Proved (short, exact, elementary symmetry argument for the expectation; concentration claim stated qualitatively, not proved with an explicit rate)
Empirical_Support: EXP_014/EXP_016 (z_m dominant 100%); EXP_017 (z_m dominant on 10/30 anomalous rounds, mixed with z_t_res)
Risk_Of_Overclaim: LOW if expectation vs per-realization distinction is preserved; MEDIUM if a reader drops the 'in expectation' qualifier and reads it as 'every Gaussian draw increases norm' -- explicitly guarded against in the source document

Title: Exact norm and cosine control of the norm-preserving directional attack
Statement_Strength: Exact equality, not approximate -- holds for every c in [-1,1] and every valid u_perp
Assumptions: u_perp is a unit vector orthogonal to Delta-hat (guaranteed by the implementation's Gram-Schmidt construction, verified against src/attacks/traceability.py); Delta != 0 (zero-update case handled separately, also exact)
Empirical_Support: delta_attack_norm_ratio and realized_cosine_to_honest verified to ~1e-10 of the exact predicted values in every directional-attack run inspected (EXP_015/018/019/024-027)
Risk_Of_Overclaim: LOW -- this is a proof about the attack's own deterministic construction, not an empirical claim about detector behavior; risk only arises if conflated with a claim about detection outcomes (kept separate via Corollary C1)

Title: Norm-only indistinguishability under exact norm preservation
Statement_Strength: Narrow and precise: about a single round's scalar norm only, given exact norm preservation (Proposition P2)
Assumptions: Decision rule f is deterministic and reads only the scalar ||Delta_{k,r}|| for one round, no history, no other feature
Proof_Status: Proved (immediate consequence of P2: identical input implies identical output for any deterministic function)
Empirical_Support: EXP_026: magnitude-only detector never confirms any client at all in the entire 50-round window (strongest empirical instance); EXP_018/EXP_015/EXP_027: magnitude-only eventually, weakly succeeds via indirect honest-counterfactual drift, consistent with the corollary's explicitly narrow scope (single-round norm only, not magnitude history)
Risk_Of_Overclaim: MEDIUM if overstated as 'magnitude-history methods always fail against this attack' -- explicitly, repeatedly scoped in the source document to single-round information only, and the empirical caveat (magnitude-only eventually succeeding in 3 of 4 runs) is stated alongside it

Title: Common-mode temporal drift cancellation via same-round median reference
Statement_Strength: Exact cancellation of the g_r term GIVEN the stated additive decomposition and median-approximation assumption; the decomposition itself is a modeling assumption consistent with observation, not derived from SGD first principles
Assumptions: Additive decomposition t_{k,r} = g_r + b_k + eta_{k,r} for honest clients; median_j(b_j+eta_{j,r}) well-approximated by a per-round constant beta_r; at most 1 arbitrary (attacker) value among n_r=5 clients (below the median's breakdown point of floor((n_r-1)/2)=2)
Proof_Status: Proved conditional on stated assumptions (exact algebra given the decomposition); the decomposition's empirical validity is not independently proved, only asserted as consistent with prior observation per research_plans/FEDTRACE_V2_TEMPORAL_CALIBRATION_PLAN.md
Empirical_Support: analysis/FEDTRACE_V3_RETROSPECTIVE_ANALYSIS.md: zero honest persistent false positives across exhaustive 49-round x 5-client check on EXP_015, the exact run whose secular-decline pattern motivated the decomposition; reproduced in EXP_016-019/026/027
Risk_Of_Overclaim: MEDIUM if the conditional nature of the decomposition assumption is dropped -- explicitly flagged in the source document as a modeling assumption consistent with observation, not a first-principles derivation from training dynamics

Title: Small-sample cross-sectional MAD instability at n=5 (v2 failure-condition analysis)
Statement_Strength: A failure-condition illustration for one specific estimator at one specific small sample size, backed by real (not constructed) numerical data -- explicitly not a general theorem about MAD estimators
Assumptions: n_r=5 same-round observations only, no historical window; illustrated with the actual EXP_015/client_000/rounds 9-11 data, not a hypothetical example
Proof_Status: Not a formal proof -- a worked numerical illustration plus a qualitative mechanism explanation (small denominator inflates an ordinary numerator)
Empirical_Support: analysis/FEDTRACE_V2_RETROSPECTIVE_ANALYSIS.md: client_000 confirmed persistent (WRONG attribution) at round 11 under FedTrace v2, exact scale/z-score values reproduced from the source document
Risk_Of_Overclaim: MEDIUM if presented as a general MAD-instability theorem rather than an illustration of one specific, verified failure episode -- explicitly scoped as non-general in the source document, and recurrence across seeds/rounds was never checked

Title: Conditional mechanistic account of temporal-consistency disruption under directional rotation
Statement_Strength: Explicitly conditional/probabilistic -- provides a plausibility argument for the observed effect, not an exact formula for z_t_res from the attack's target cosine c
Assumptions: u_perp independent of, and with high probability not aligned with, the orthogonal component of Delta_{r-1} relative to Delta_r (a high-dimensional concentration argument, not proved with an explicit rate); explicitly does NOT assume the attack controls cos(Delta_attack, Delta_{r-1}) directly (it does not -- verified against src/attacks/traceability.py, which enforces cosine against the CURRENT honest update only)
Proof_Status: Not proved -- a conditional mechanistic derivation with an explicit disclaimer that no exact formula is claimed
Empirical_Support: self_prev_round_cosine collapses to near-zero magnitude immediately at onset in every directional-attack trace inspected (EXP_015/018/019/024-027)
Risk_Of_Overclaim: HIGH if misread as an exact derivation of z_t_res from c -- the source document explicitly refuses to provide one and states this risk directly; must retain the 'conditional mechanistic remark, not a guarantee' framing in any paper use

Title: Persistence-delay lemma
Statement_Strength: Exact and tight: proves both the achieved delay under a fully-contiguous P-round anomalous run AND that no P-round contiguous-persistence rule can do better
Assumptions: A client's raw anomaly score is strictly above threshold at every round in a contiguous P-round window starting at the true onset
Proof_Status: Proved (direct, 4-line argument from the persistence algorithm's own definition)
Empirical_Support: EXP_016/017/018/019/026/027: onset_error=0 and detection_delay=2 (the P-1=2 minimum) in all 6 successful attribution runs, exactly, not merely approximately
Risk_Of_Overclaim: LOW -- this is an exact statement about the frozen algorithm's own mechanics, not an empirical or statistical claim; overclaim risk only if 'minimum possible delay under this rule' is misread as 'minimum possible delay under any detector design'

Title: Structural distinction between per-round robust aggregation and longitudinal forensic attribution
Statement_Strength: A definitional/structural observation about function domains (Agg_r reads only round r; Attr reads the full history) -- not a theorem that any specific aggregator fails at attribution
Assumptions: Agg_r is defined as a function of only the current round's cross-section (true by construction for Multi-Krum, verified against src/federated/aggregation/multikrum.py); Attr is defined as a function of the full accumulated history (true by construction for FedTrace v3, Part 3)
Proof_Status: Proved as a structural/definitional fact about the two function signatures; not a theorem about robust aggregators in general
Empirical_Support: EXP_020-025: Multi-Krum's full-run rejection-persistence proxy misattributes the honest largest-partition client in all 4 attacked runs and never once corrects for the directional family, offered as one concrete evidencing instance
Risk_Of_Overclaim: MEDIUM if generalized beyond Multi-Krum to 'no robust aggregator can ever support attribution' -- explicitly scoped as a structural observation illustrated by, not proved via, the Multi-Krum evidence

Title: Multi-Krum geometric failure-condition analysis under norm-preserving directional attack
Statement_Strength: A failure-condition / geometric-intuition statement, explicitly not a universal theorem about Krum-family robustness
Assumptions: n=5, f=1 (this project's fixed configuration); strong Non-IID heterogeneity (alpha=0.1) already producing a large honest-population pairwise-distance spread (established independently by EXP_009); attack severity fixed at c=0 (exact orthogonality)
Proof_Status: Not proved as a general theorem -- a mechanistic decomposition (d(i,j) via norm and cosine terms) plus a qualitative sufficient-condition argument, directly evidenced by the empirical 2x2 factorial result
Empirical_Support: EXP_022-025: 100%/100% Gaussian-family rejection vs 0%/0% directional-family rejection, both seeds, a fully-crossed 2x2 result with zero exceptions
Risk_Of_Overclaim: HIGH if read as 'Multi-Krum (or Krum-family scoring) is blind to all norm-preserving attacks' -- explicitly restricted to this project's tested configuration (one f, one n, one heterogeneity level, one rotation severity) and stated as such in the source document
